title: Hybrid protocol load fabric for realistic chat streaming
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a flexible, protocol-agnostic load fabric that can generate realistic chat/completion traffic patterns across SSE and WebSocket clients. The fabric must simulate token-emission behavior (bursty and steady), connection churn, mid-stream cancellations, reconnections, and multi-turn chat context growth so that service-level p95 latency and tokens/sec throughput are measured under realistic conditions. The goal is to provide deterministic, reproducible scenarios for: (1) capacity planning, (2) regression detection for p95 increases or token throughput regressions, and (3) validation of KV cache/cold-start effects on streaming sessions. This ticket covers design, implementation, monitoring hooks, and a first set of regression gates and dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: A protocol layer that can emit identical scenarios over SSE and WebSocket with a single scenario definition file.
Built-in token-level pacing controls: per-session tokens/sec, burst windows, and jitter parameters.

Metrics emitted to our observability stack: tokens_emitted_total, stream_p95_latency_ms, stream_error_rate, connection_reconnects_total, avg_kv_cache_hit_ratio; metrics use consistent tag keys (route, model_variant, region, test_scenario).
Regression detector job that runs nightly comparing latest run to baseline; raises alert if p95 latency increases by >20% or tokens/sec drops by >15% for a route.

At least three canonical scenarios implemented: short-chat churn (many short sessions), long-context steady (few long sessions with growing context), and bursty-traffic mix (mixed session lengths with intermittent large bursts).
End-to-end runbooks and a dashboard (perf: Streaming Load / Hybrid Fabric) with links to raw traces, token timeline heatmaps, and per-test artifacts.
Automated CI step that runs a lightweight smoke version of each scenario on PRs touching runtime or streaming codepaths.
tasks: Design scenario definition language (YAML) and implement parser (schema, examples).
Implement protocol adapters: lightweight SSE client harness and WS harness sharing the same scenario engine.
Add token-level pacing engine with configurable distribution (poisson, fixed-rate, burst windows) and mid-stream cancellation signals.
Integrate metric exporters (Prometheus) and event traces to the existing perf namespace; ensure tags include model_variant and route.
Create regression detector job using persisted baselines and write alerting rules (PagerDuty + Slack channel).
Wire up dashboard panels and notebook examples for debugging failed runs.
Add CI smoke test and document usage for performance team and SREs.
metrics: stream_p95_latency_ms (end-to-end from first client byte to final server byte)
